definition: Intel's Deep Learning Boost (DL Boost) is a marketing name for instruction set architecture (ISA) features on the x86-64 designed to improve performance on deep learning tasks such as training and inference..
details: Intel's Deep Learning Boost (DL Boost) is a marketing name for instruction set architecture (ISA) features on the x86-64 designed to improve performance on deep learning tasks such as training and inference.

explainer.lead: Intel DL Boost is a name for features added to the x86-64 instruction set to improve deep learning performance. It targets both training models and running them for inference, using processor capabilities rather than a separate model or software library.

tiers.eli5: It is like adding special kitchen tools to a standard stove so everyday cooking tasks go faster.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on it indirectly through frameworks and libraries compiled to use these instructions. A pitfall is that speedups depend on the specific CPU generation and on whether the software stack actually targets these instructions.
tiers.paperLevel: DL Boost denotes instruction set architecture features on x86-64 aimed at improving deep learning training and inference performance. Limits: it is a marketing name covering ISA features, and real gains vary by processor and workload.

usedIn.name: Intel x86-64 processors
usedIn.detail: Provide the instruction-set features collected under the DL Boost name.

usedIn.name: Deep learning training
usedIn.detail: Model-training workloads are one of the performance targets.

usedIn.name: Deep learning inference
usedIn.detail: Running trained models to produce predictions is another target.

components.name: x86-64 ISA features
components.detail: Processor instruction-set features marketed together as DL Boost.

components.name: Training workload support
components.detail: Features intended to improve performance while models learn from data.

components.name: Inference workload support
components.detail: Features intended to improve performance when trained models produce outputs.

flow: A deep learning training or inference task runs on a compatible Intel x86-64 processor.
The software uses the instruction-set features identified as DL Boost.
Those features are designed to improve the workload's performance.
explainer.origin: Intel created the DL Boost name for deep-learning-oriented instruction set features on x86-64.
explainer.whyItMatters: DL Boost connects deep learning performance to capabilities in the processor itself. It is relevant to both sides of a model's life cycle: learning from data and producing predictions afterward.

diagram.caption: DL Boost sits at the instruction-set level, supporting deep learning training and inference workloads.

explainer.example: Inference on an Intel CPU with DL Boost runs faster when the framework is built to use the relevant vector instructions.
